articles.summary: Katy Watson explores Australia's relationship with China - partner, rival or 'frenemy'?
articles.body:
World Service , · 17 Sep 2026 , · 26 mins

Katy Watson highlights Australia’s complex, turbulent and evolving relationship with their number one trading partner - China. Having signed a free trade agreement eleven years ago, in recent years there has been a marked shift in relations, with Canberra balancing its security dependence on Washington with its economic reliance on Beijing. From businesses, diplomats and military personnel, Katy Watson asks if China is Australia’s enemy or friend? Or as some critics suggest, are they a ‘frenemy’? Presenter: Katy Watson Producer: Peter Shevlin A Pod60 production for BBC World Service

articles.title: South Korean restaurant owner avoids jail time in ‘ants on a plate’ accusation
articles.summary: The owner of a two-Michelin-star restaurant in Seoul must pay an $11,000 for serving an edible ant dessert.
articles.body: The owner of a two-Michelin-starred restaurant in South Korea has avoided prison time in a highly publicized case surrounding a sorbet dessert topped with ants. On September 16, the Seoul Western District Court fined the owner of the restaurant 15 million won ($11,000). The owner was identified only as a woman with the last name Kim, and the restaurant was not publicly named. The restaurant’s chef was not charged with any wrongdoing. Prosecutors had sought a one-year jail term for the owner and a 20 million won ($13,580) fine, citing a profit of 120 million won ($81,470) over the past four years. The problem isn’t that insects appeared on the menu. Rather, the issue is South Korea’s nuanced food laws, which regulate which insects can go on diners’ plates. In July, the prosecutor’s office told CNN that the eatery in question has been serving dried ants brought in from the US and Thailand since 2021. They alleged that the restaurant had served about 49,000 ants in 12,200 sherbet dishes. According to the government, it wasn’t merely the presence of ants in food that was an issue. The Ministry of Food and Drug Safety said investigators “found the ants from this restaurant contained heavy metal levels up to 55 times the maximum limit allowed for other edible insects.” In making his ruling, the judge noted that there was a potential health risk because heavy metals above the permitted level were found in ants sold by the restaurant. However, when determining the sentence, the judge took into account that the amount of ants used appeared to be less than the amount calculated by prosecutors, and that Kim had no prior criminal record. Advocates in South Korea and elsewhere have increasingly argued that insects are just as reliable a source of protein as other animal products. Given how easily they are raised and harvested with fewer resources than are needed for more traditional livestock, insects present an effective way to combat climate change. South Korean cuisine doesn’t frown on insects. Beondegi, for example, is a traditional steamed silkworm pupa snack served by street vendors in paper cups. But under the country’s Food Sanitation Act, only 10 insect species, including grasshoppers and silkworms, are permitted for human consumption. Serving any other insect — like ants — requires special approval from authorities. Lawyers representing the restaurant said its chef used ants to add acidity to the dish, without realizing that the recipe he once used in the US and Europe is legally banned in South Korea, local media reported. They also said the restaurant only served ants to about 60% of the customers and that the ants were clearly identified on the menu as part of the dish. According to a 2013 report by the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization, at least two billion people worldwide already eat bugs every day. The most commonly eaten insect groups globally are ants, beetles, bees, caterpillars, cicadas, crickets, dragonflies, flies, grasshoppers, leaf bugs, locusts, scale insects, termites and wasps, according to the FAO. The trend has gained traction in Europe and the United States in recent years: a report by Global Market Insights previously projected the US edible insect market would grow to nearly $80 million by 2024, with Europe also logging growth. Among those avidly promoting edible insects in the West is New York City-based chef Joseph Yoon, executive director of Brooklyn Bugs, an organization that wants to change diners’ perceptions of creepy crawlies. Yoon has made tarantula tempura and caramel popcorn with grasshoppers in his work as a guest chef and advocate. In Copenhagen, Alchemist, a two-Michelin-starred establishment currently ranked No. 5 on The World’s 50 Best Restaurants list, teamed up with scientists to ferment dairy products with the help of both live and frozen ants. It resulted in a popular “ant-wich,” ice cream sandwiched between ant-shaped cookies with an ant-infused gel.

articles.title: Premiê do Canadá diz aceitar convite da UE e alfineta Trump | G1
articles.standfirst: Canadá foi convidado nesta semana para se tornar 1º 'membro associado' da UE. Mark Carney disse que movimento não se trata de formar um novo bloco para rivalizar com potências, e sim sobre resiliência. Presidente dos EUA criticou associação.
articles.summary: Canadá foi convidado nesta semana para se tornar 1º 'membro associado' da UE. Mark Carney disse que movimento não se trata de formar um novo bloco para rivalizar com potências, e sim sobre resiliência. Presidente dos EUA criticou associação.
articles.body:
Presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, junto com primeiro-ministro do Canadá, Mark Carney, após discurso do canadense no Parlamento europeu em Strasburgo, na França, em 17 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Yves Herman

O primeiro-ministro do Canadá , Mark Carney , afirmou nesta quinta-feira (17) que aceitou o convite da União Europeia para se tornar "membro associado" do bloco e alfinetou o governo Trump ao dizer que "ninguém ditará com quem fazemos acordo".

Carney disse que a associação à UE "é algo positivo, não uma reação", e que "um Canadá mais forte e resiliente seria um parceiro mais efetivo para os Estados Unidos". No entanto, sobre as críticas do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump , ele enfatizou que "ninguém vai ditar com quem nós [Canadá] fazemos acordos".

Na quarta-feira, Trump ridicularizou o convite da UE ao Canadá , classificando-o como “cômico”, e fez ameaças caso a movimentação de fato aconteça. “Se eles fizerem isso e se eu considerar que se trata de algum tipo de ato hostil, vou impor tarifas muito pesadas ou interromper o comércio com a Europa em muitas áreas”, afirmou.

Trump tem incitado uma crise diplomática com o Canadá durante seu 2º mandato na Casa Branca, com tarifas e ameaças à soberania do vizinho, o que fez com que o governo canadense se sentisse ameaçado. Além disso, tanto a UE quanto o Canadá têm enfrentado forte concorrência e pressão do governo de Trump em questões comerciais, entre outras, e de uma China cada vez mais assertiva.

Carney também disse nesta quinta que Canadá e União Europeia "são mais fortes juntos" e que a associação não se trata sobre a criação de um novo bloco geopolítico nem rivalizar com potências mundiais, e sim "para que ninguém nos subjugue" .

"Não buscamos poder para dominar os outros, pelo contrário, buscamos resiliência e autonomia para que ninguém e nem possa controlar nossos mercados abertos, prejudicar nossa soberania, ameaçar nossa integridade territorial ou minar nossas liberdades, nossas democracias e nosso Estado de Direito", afirmou o premiê canadense.

Carney discursou e deu uma coletiva de imprensa no Parlamento europeu um dia após a presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, ter convidado seu país para se tornar o 1º "membro associado" da UE, algo inédito na história do bloco. O premiê canadense foi ovacionado diversas vezes pelos parlamentares presentes durante sua fala.

Carney afirmou também que a entrada do Canadá na UE como "membro associado" ainda será debatida e votada pelo Parlamento canadense , que terá a última palavra sobre se a associação ocorrerá ou não.

articles.title: 12 das 22 empresas de ônibus que operam em São Paulo são suspeitas de ligação com o PCC; veja quais são elas | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresas de ônibus foram alvo da Operação Vectura Corrupta, realizada pela Polícia Civil e pelo MP-SP na manhã desta quinta-feira (17).
articles.summary: Empresas de ônibus foram alvo da Operação Vectura Corrupta, da Polícia Civil e do MP-SP. Do total de 1.331 linhas da cidade, 511 são do grupo investigado.
articles.body:
Veículos da empresa Move Buss, que operam linhas na cidade de São Paulo e são alvo de operação do MP-SP. — Foto: Divulgação/Redes Sociais

Doze das 22 empresas de ônibus que operam na cidade de São Paulo são suspeitas de ligação com a facção criminosa Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC), segundo o Ministério Público de São Paulo.

Elas foram alvo da Operação Vectura Corrupta, realizada pela Polícia Civil e pelo MP-SP na manhã desta quinta-feira (17), que também tem como alvo o ex-vereador Milton Leite (União Brasil), também ex-presidente da Câmara Municipal, e o ex-presidente da SPTrans, Levi dos Santos Oliveira. (leia mais abaixo)

Essas empresas investigadas possuem mais da metade de todo o sistema de ônibus da capital paulista, que é o maior da América Latina e está entre os cinco maiores do mundo.

Criadas a partir de cooperativas de transportes, operam no chamado subsistema local, dos bairros mais afastados. Este subsistema responde por 6.029 ônibus da frota total de 13.690 veículos.

Veja abaixo as empresas que fazem parte das investigações da Operação Vectura Corrupta:

A Transwolff — com outra empresa de ônibus, a UPBus — já tinha sido alvo de outra operação, a Fim da Linha, deflagrada em abril de 2024 pelo MP-SP por suspeita de lavagem de dinheiro e favorecimento ao PCC.

As investigações apontam que o dinheiro usado para aumentar o capital da Transwolff poderia ter origem ilícita — ou seja, os recursos seriam provenientes de atividades do PCC.

O esquema envolveria uso de “laranjas” e “CNPJs fantasmas”, facilidades de empresas de fachada para ocultar as verdadeiras origens dos valores, algo típico de lavagem de dinheiro.

Em função dessas suspeitas, a Prefeitura de São Paulo rescindiu os contratos e assumiu o controle da Transwolff e da UPBus em dezembro de 2024. O prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB) afirmou que não há nenhum risco de ligação com o PCC. "Fiz a intervenção em 2024 na TrasWolf e caducidade, esse empresa é administrada pela prefeitura", afirmou.

Milton Leite não foi encontrado pelos policiais que foram à sua casa para cumprir o mandado. Segundo apurou a GloboNews, a polícia passou a considerá-lo foragido diante das circunstâncias encontradas no imóvel. Policiais permanecem no local para cumprir mandado de busca e apreensão.

De acordo com informações obtidas durante a diligência, Milton estava em casa até a tarde de quarta-feira (16). Uma funcionária relatou aos policiais que ele saiu à noite para um compromisso de campanha.

Também foram presos Levi dos Santos Oliveira, ex-presidente da SPTrans, e Danilo Marco Morgado Silva, ex-candidato à Prefeitura de Praia Grande e atual candidato a deputado estadual.

Em nota, Milton Leite afirmou que está viajando e negou estar foragido. “Estou em viagem, não estou foragido, e vou me apresentar às autoridades em até 24 horas. Vou provar minha inocência em todas as acusações”, declarou o ex-vereador.

Ao todo, a operação busca cumprir 16 mandados de prisão e 18 de busca e apreensão em São Paulo, Santana de Parnaíba, São Bernardo do Campo, Diadema, Santos, Praia Grande e Cubatão.

Buscas na casa de Milton Leite — Foto: TV Globo

Investigação aponta influência de Milton Leite no setor de ônibus

Segundo apuração da GloboNews, a investigação aponta que decisões estratégicas relacionadas a empresas de transporte suspeitas de ligação com o PCC dependeriam do conhecimento ou da aprovação política de Milton Leite. A conclusão foi sustentada, segundo investigadores, pela análise de interceptações envolvendo operadores e por elementos de outras investigações relacionadas ao papel decisório do ex-vereador.

No pedido que embasou a operação, Milton Leite é citado como responsável direto pela operação de algumas das empresas que, segundo a investigação, seriam controladas pela facção. O documento também menciona declarações de policiais militares, prestadas em procedimento no Tribunal de Justiça Militar, segundo as quais ele seria o dono de fato da Transwolff.

Milton Leite deixou a vida pública no ano passado , depois de sete mandatos como vereador e de ter presidido a Câmara Municipal por quatro vezes. Atualmente, ele é presidente do União Brasil na cidade de São Paulo. Em julho, foi eleito presidente estadual da Federação União Progressista (UP), formada pelo União Brasil e pelo Progressistas (PP).

A Operação Vectura Corrupta é realizada pela Delegacia de Investigações Sobre Entorpecentes de Mogi das Cruzes, com apoio do Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco), do Ministério Público de São Paulo.

Milton Leite (União Brasil), ex-presidente da Câmara de SP — Foto: Paulo Gomes/TV Globo

Entre os presos está Levi dos Santos Oliveira, ex-presidente da SPTrans. Segundo os investigadores, apesar de Levi não aparecer como interlocutor direto de José Daniel Satilite, apontado como um dos personagens centrais do esquema, os dois teriam mantido encontros periódicos.

A investigação afirma que essas reuniões tinham como finalidade tratar de interesses da facção relacionados a empresas de transporte, especialmente após a deflagração da Operação Fim da Linha pelo Ministério Público de São Paulo, em 2024.

A defesa de Levi dos Santos Oliveira diz que ele não tem antecedentes, construiu ao longo de décadas, uma trajetória de relevantes serviços públicos prestados à cidade de São Paulo, atuando na SPTrans, onde se consolidou como referência técnica em sua área.

Outra frente da operação chegou a Danilo Marco Morgado Silva, que disputou a Prefeitura de Praia Grande em 2024 e era candidato a deputado estadual, mas teve o registro cassado . Ele também foi preso nesta quinta.

Danilo já havia sido alvo de mandado de busca e apreensão na Operação Decurio. Segundo a Polícia Civil, a nova etapa da investigação identificou um "forte vínculo" dele com integrantes do PCC e indícios de que sua campanha à prefeitura teria sido financiada pela organização criminosa.

Outra frente da operação investiga a chamada "Sintonia dos Gravatas", núcleo formado por advogados que, segundo a polícia, atuaria diretamente em benefício da organização criminosa, ultrapassando os limites do exercício profissional da advocacia.

Entre os investigados estão Cícero José dos Santos Filho, Eduardo Medeiros e Milton Mello Milreu. Segundo a investigação, escritórios e contas bancárias teriam sido utilizados para reuniões, movimentações financeiras e outras atividades de interesse da facção.

O principal investigado apontado nesta fase é José Daniel Satilite, conhecido como Alemão. A Polícia Civil afirma que ele integra o PCC e funcionaria como intermediário entre empresários, advogados, políticos, pessoas próximas a políticos e integrantes da facção.

O avanço de hoje é um desdobramento direto de duas operações anteriores. Em abril de 2026, a Polícia Civil e o Ministério Público realizaram a Operação Contaminatio , focada na estrutura de uma fintech gerida pela facção. O objetivo do grupo era usar a empresa de tecnologia financeira para se infiltrar em prefeituras e assumir o gerenciamento do recebimento de tributos, taxas e o contato direto com os munícipes. Naquela etapa, a investigação desarticulou a rede de doleiros e de operadores de criptoativos usada na lavagem do dinheiro e prendeu um ex-vereador de Santo André.

Toda a apuração teve início em agosto de 2024, com a Operação Decurio . Após a apreensão de 30 quilos de drogas em Itaquaquecetuba, os investigadores extraíram dados do celular da mulher de um dos líderes da facção. As informações do aparelho levaram à identificação e prisão de chefes da chamada "Sintonia Final" e à descoberta da fintech, que chegou a movimentar cerca de R$ 8 bilhões.

Foi também na primeira fase que surgiram as evidências iniciais do braço político da organização, com a identificação de campanhas de vereadores patrocinadas pela facção e o envolvimento de servidores comissionados em prefeituras do estado.

articles.title: Why is inflation rising again around the world?
articles.summary: Rising energy prices are pushing inflation higher again, forcing major central banks to raise interest rates.
articles.body:
For decades, central banks treated oil shocks as temporary, something to wait out, not hike rates over.

And that’s because raising rates in this case can slow growth without bringing down the price of a single barrel of oil.

Oil surged past $100 a barrel last week.

Six months into the Iran war, the Strait of Hormuz remains disrupted and Houthi advances threaten Saudi oil supplies, too.

Energy costs are feeding through into household and business bills.

That is forcing policymakers to reconsider the old rulebook even though tighter policy means higher borrowing costs.

articles.title: Prepara Lojista ajuda comerciantes com vendas de fim de ano em MT | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento será realizado nesta quinta-feira (17), às 19h, no Rotary Club. Palestra vai abordar estratégias de vendas, marketing, atendimento e fidelização de clientes.
articles.summary: Evento será realizado nesta quinta-feira (17), às 19h, no Rotary Club. Palestra vai abordar estratégias de vendas, marketing, atendimento e fidelização de clientes.
articles.body:
Cidade de Cáceres (MT) — Foto: Reprodução

Empresários e comerciantes de Cáceres , a 220 km de Cuiabá, poderão participar, nesta quinta-feira (17), de uma palestra gratuita com estratégias para aumentar as vendas e melhorar o atendimento ao cliente durante o período de fim de ano .

O evento faz parte do Prepara Lojista 2026 e será realizado às 19h, no Rotary Club de Cáceres. A palestra será ministrada pelo especialista em estratégias de vendas Dino Gueno .

A iniciativa é da TV Centro América , com realização do Senac Mato Grosso e apoio da Câmara de Dirigentes Lojistas (CDL) de Cáceres e do Rotary Club Cáceres.

A proposta do encontro é ajudar os comerciantes a se prepararem para o aumento do movimento nas lojas durante as vendas de fim de ano. Entre os assuntos que serão abordados estão:

técnicas para melhorar o atendimento e a experiência dos consumidores;

recuperação de clientes que passaram a comprar na concorrência;

Segundo o consultor comercial do Senac em Cáceres, Bruno José Duarte Brandão, a falta de planejamento para o período de maior movimento pode prejudicar os resultados dos estabelecimentos.

A orientação é que os empresários se preparem não apenas para receber um número maior de consumidores, mas também para oferecer um atendimento capaz de transformar esse movimento em vendas e melhorar o faturamento no fim do ano.

A consultora comercial Andreia Sabrina Nascimento ressaltou que a palestra apresentará ferramentas que podem ser usadas pelos lojistas para manter os consumidores e recuperar antigos clientes.

Evento para empresários e lojistas com especialistas em vendas Dino Gueno — Foto: Reprodução

Cáceres é a segunda cidade a receber o Prepara Lojista nesta semana. Na terça-feira (15), o evento foi realizado em Tangará da Serra .

A programação percorre cidades de Mato Grosso com orientações e estratégias que podem ser aplicadas no dia a dia dos estabelecimentos, especialmente com a proximidade das vendas de fim de ano.

O corpo do pescador foi liberado ao serviço funerário após os trabalhos dos bombeiros.

articles.title: Investigação diz que Milton Leite é 'dono de fato' da Transwolff em SP | G1
articles.standfirst: Por meio de nota, a Transwolff diz que 'Milton Leite nunca teve qualquer participação societária, nunca participou da gestão ou ‘deu ordens’'.
articles.summary: Por meio de nota, a Transwolff diz que 'Milton Leite nunca teve qualquer participação societária, nunca participou da gestão ou ‘deu ordens’'.
articles.body:
O ex-vereador Milton Leite (União Brasil) é apontado como dono de fato da TransWolff em São Paulo. — Foto: Montagem/g1/André Bueno/Rede Câmara

A intervenção foi determinada por Nunes por meio do Decreto Municipal nº 63.328, de 9 de abril de 2024. A medida também atingiu, na época, a empresa UPBus .

Após a intervenção da Prefeitura de SP, as linhas da Zona Sul da capital antes operadas pela Transwolff foram transferidas para as empresas Sancetur e Alfa RodoBus. Essa segunda também é acusada de ligação com o crime organizado.

Alfa RodoBus e Transwolff constam na lista de 12 viações de ônibus que foram alvo, nesta quinta-feira (17), da chamada Operação Vectura Corrupta , que investiga a infiltração do PCC no transporte público da capital paulista.

Na decisão do desembargador Sérgio Antônio Ribas, que autorizou as investigações e os mandados de prisão pedidos pelo Ministério Público de São Paulo , a Transwolff é citada como tendo como “dono oculto e de fato” o ex-presidente da Câmara Municipal de São Paulo, Milton Leite ( União Brasil ).

“Milton Leite da Silva é citado nominalmente [nas investigações] por diversas vezes como responsável direto pela operação de algumas das empresas controladas pelo PCC. Somado a isso há declarações de policiais militares em procedimento junto ao Tribunal de Justiça Militar, que o mesmo seria o dono de fato da empresa Transwolf", disse Sérgio Ribas.

Milton Leite (União Brasil) era braço direito do prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB) antes de se aposentar. — Foto: Divulgação/PMSP

O desembargador decretou a prisão temporária de Milton Leite por 30 dias. Ele está sendo procurado pela polícia e diz que está viajando, mas vai se entregar às autoridades.

“Estou em viagem, não estou foragido, e vou me apresentar às autoridades em até 24 horas. Nego veementemente todas as acusações e vou provar minha inocência”, disse o presidente do União Brasil por meio de nota.

“A minha atuação em relação ao setor de transportes se deu a pedido do então prefeito Bruno Covas, em 2019, já que naquela ocasião, como presidente da Câmara, eu ocupava também a função de vice-prefeito na linha sucessória. É público, inclusive, que eu atuei em negociações envolvendo greves no setor”, declarou Leite.

Policiais e dois promotores fizeram buscas nos endereços de Milton Leite e saíram de lá com malotes de documentos.

Questionado sobre o risco de a operação afetar o transporte público da capital, o prefeito Ricardo Nunes ( MDB ) afirmou que **não há risco de interrupção do serviço**. Segundo ele, a prefeitura fez a intervenção na Transwolff em 2024 e posteriormente decretou a caducidade do contrato. “Nenhum risco. Fiz a intervenção em 2024 na Transwolff e [decretei a] caducidade. Essa empresa é administrada pela prefeitura”, afirmou.

Por meio de nota, a Transwolff diz que “Milton Leite nunca teve qualquer participação societária na Transwolff, nunca participou da gestão ou ‘deu ordens’ na empresa e se reputa que tal afirmação está completamente equivocada e dissociada da realidade”.

“O empresário Luiz Carlos Efigenio Pacheco nunca havia sido denunciado em nenhuma outra situação em sua vida até as indevidas imputações da 'Operação Fim de Linha', que estão sendo combatidas na Justiça, com a defesa alegando sua total inocência. O processo administrativo de intervenção ilegal e arbitrário na Transwolff está sendo questionado na Justiça”, diz a empresa.

“Ressalta-se que o decreto de intervenção da Prefeitura se apoia exclusivamente em questões financeiras, comuns a todas as empresas do setor e plenamente sanáveis, não havendo qualquer fundamento criminal, diferentemente do que havia sido inicialmente aventado na intervenção”, afirmou.

A Alfa RodoBus Transportes já operava no sistema municipal de São Paulo antes da crise envolvendo Transwolff e UPBus. A empresa é concessionária do lote D13, no subsistema local de distribuição da cidade.

A empresa operava com 148 ônibus, atendendo cerca de 90,3 mil passageiros por dia na região Oeste da cidade.

Documentos do Tribunal de Contas do Município (TCM) mostram que a Alfa RodoBus era titular do contrato de concessão do lote D13, com valor contratual de aproximadamente R$ 1,62 bilhão no acordo assinado com a SPTrans em 2019.

A empresa não foi alvo da Operação Fim da Linha, em abril de 2024, mas está na lista de 12 empresas investigadas da Operação Vectura Corrupta, após assumir as operações da UPBus, na Zona Leste de São Paulo.

Após a saída da UPBus do sistema, a Alfa RodoBus assumiu 13 novas linhas na região Leste.

Veículos da empresa Move Buss, que operam linhas na cidade de São Paulo e são alvo de operação do MP-SP. — Foto: Divulgação/Redes Sociais

Doze das 22 empresas de ônibus que operam na cidade de São Paulo são suspeitas de ligação com a facção criminosa Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC), segundo o Ministério Público de São Paulo.

Elas foram alvo da Operação Vectura Corrupta, que também tem como alvo o ex-vereador Milton Leite (União Brasil) e o ex-presidente da SPTrans, Levi dos Santos Oliveira, que foi preso . (leia mais abaixo)

Essas empresas investigadas possuem mais da metade de todo o sistema de ônibus da capital paulista, que é o maior da América Latina e está entre os cinco maiores do mundo.

Criadas a partir de cooperativas de transportes, operam no chamado subsistema local, dos bairros mais afastados. Este subsistema responde por 6.029 ônibus da frota total de 13.690 veículos.

Veja abaixo as empresas que fazem parte das investigações da Operação Vectura Corrupta:

A Transwolff — com outra empresa de ônibus, a UPBus — já tinha sido alvo de outra operação, a Fim da Linha, deflagrada em abril de 2024 pelo MP-SP por suspeita de lavagem de dinheiro e favorecimento ao PCC.

As investigações apontam que o dinheiro usado para aumentar o capital da Transwolff poderia ter origem ilícita — ou seja, os recursos seriam provenientes de atividades do PCC.

O esquema envolveria uso de “laranjas” e “CNPJs fantasmas”, facilidades de empresas de fachada para ocultar as verdadeiras origens dos valores, algo típico de lavagem de dinheiro.

Em função dessas suspeitas, a Prefeitura de São Paulo rescindiu os contratos e assumiu o controle da Transwolff e da UPBus em dezembro de 2024. O prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB) afirmou que não há nenhum risco de ligação com o PCC. "Fiz a intervenção em 2024 na TrasWolf e caducidade, esse empresa é administrada pela prefeitura", afirmou.

Milton Leite não foi encontrado pelos policiais que foram à sua casa para cumprir o mandado. Segundo apurou a GloboNews, a polícia passou a considerá-lo foragido diante das circunstâncias encontradas no imóvel. Policiais permanecem no local para cumprir mandado de busca e apreensão.

De acordo com informações obtidas durante a diligência, Milton estava em casa até a tarde de quarta-feira (16). Uma funcionária relatou aos policiais que ele saiu à noite para um compromisso de campanha.

Também foram presos Levi dos Santos Oliveira, ex-presidente da SPTrans, e Danilo Marco Morgado Silva, ex-candidato à Prefeitura de Praia Grande e atual candidato a deputado estadual.

Em nota, Milton Leite afirmou que está viajando e negou estar foragido. “Estou em viagem, não estou foragido, e vou me apresentar às autoridades em até 24 horas. Vou provar minha inocência em todas as acusações”, declarou o ex-vereador.

Ao todo, a operação busca cumprir 16 mandados de prisão e 18 de busca e apreensão em São Paulo, Santana de Parnaíba, São Bernardo do Campo, Diadema, Santos, Praia Grande e Cubatão.

Buscas na casa de Milton Leite — Foto: TV Globo

Investigação aponta influência de Milton Leite no setor de ônibus

Segundo apuração da GloboNews, a investigação aponta que decisões estratégicas relacionadas a empresas de transporte suspeitas de ligação com o PCC dependeriam do conhecimento ou da aprovação política de Milton Leite. A conclusão foi sustentada, segundo investigadores, pela análise de interceptações envolvendo operadores e por elementos de outras investigações relacionadas ao papel decisório do ex-vereador.

No pedido que embasou a operação, Milton Leite é citado como responsável direto pela operação de algumas das empresas que, segundo a investigação, seriam controladas pela facção. O documento também menciona declarações de policiais militares, prestadas em procedimento no Tribunal de Justiça Militar, segundo as quais ele seria o dono de fato da Transwolff.

Milton Leite deixou a vida pública no ano passado , depois de sete mandatos como vereador e de ter presidido a Câmara Municipal por quatro vezes. Atualmente, ele é presidente do União Brasil na cidade de São Paulo. Em julho, foi eleito presidente estadual da Federação União Progressista (UP), formada pelo União Brasil e pelo Progressistas (PP).

A Operação Vectura Corrupta é realizada pela Delegacia de Investigações Sobre Entorpecentes de Mogi das Cruzes, com apoio do Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco), do Ministério Público de São Paulo.

Milton Leite (União Brasil), ex-presidente da Câmara de SP — Foto: Paulo Gomes/TV Globo

Entre os presos está Levi dos Santos Oliveira, ex-presidente da SPTrans. Segundo os investigadores, apesar de Levi não aparecer como interlocutor direto de José Daniel Satilite, apontado como um dos personagens centrais do esquema, os dois teriam mantido encontros periódicos.

A investigação afirma que essas reuniões tinham como finalidade tratar de interesses da facção relacionados a empresas de transporte, especialmente após a deflagração da Operação Fim da Linha pelo Ministério Público de São Paulo, em 2024.

A defesa de Levi dos Santos Oliveira diz que ele não tem antecedentes, construiu ao longo de décadas, uma trajetória de relevantes serviços públicos prestados à cidade de São Paulo, atuando na SPTrans, onde se consolidou como referência técnica em sua área.

Outra frente da operação chegou a Danilo Marco Morgado Silva, que disputou a Prefeitura de Praia Grande em 2024 e era candidato a deputado estadual, mas teve o registro cassado . Ele também foi preso nesta quinta.

Danilo já havia sido alvo de mandado de busca e apreensão na Operação Decurio. Segundo a Polícia Civil, a nova etapa da investigação identificou um "forte vínculo" dele com integrantes do PCC e indícios de que sua campanha à prefeitura teria sido financiada pela organização criminosa.

Outra frente da operação investiga a chamada "Sintonia dos Gravatas", núcleo formado por advogados que, segundo a polícia, atuaria diretamente em benefício da organização criminosa, ultrapassando os limites do exercício profissional da advocacia.

Entre os investigados estão Cícero José dos Santos Filho, Eduardo Medeiros e Milton Mello Milreu. Segundo a investigação, escritórios e contas bancárias teriam sido utilizados para reuniões, movimentações financeiras e outras atividades de interesse da facção.

O principal investigado apontado nesta fase é José Daniel Satilite, conhecido como Alemão. A Polícia Civil afirma que ele integra o PCC e funcionaria como intermediário entre empresários, advogados, políticos, pessoas próximas a políticos e integrantes da facção.

O avanço de hoje é um desdobramento direto de duas operações anteriores. Em abril de 2026, a Polícia Civil e o Ministério Público realizaram a Operação Contaminatio , focada na estrutura de uma fintech gerida pela facção. O objetivo do grupo era usar a empresa de tecnologia financeira para se infiltrar em prefeituras e assumir o gerenciamento do recebimento de tributos, taxas e o contato direto com os munícipes. Naquela etapa, a investigação desarticulou a rede de doleiros e de operadores de criptoativos usada na lavagem do dinheiro e prendeu um ex-vereador de Santo André.

Toda a apuração teve início em agosto de 2024, com a Operação Decurio . Após a apreensão de 30 quilos de drogas em Itaquaquecetuba, os investigadores extraíram dados do celular da mulher de um dos líderes da facção. As informações do aparelho levaram à identificação e prisão de chefes da chamada "Sintonia Final" e à descoberta da fintech, que chegou a movimentar cerca de R$ 8 bilhões.

Foi também na primeira fase que surgiram as evidências iniciais do braço político da organização, com a identificação de campanhas de vereadores patrocinadas pela facção e o envolvimento de servidores comissionados em prefeituras do estado.

articles.title: Why is London's mobile phone reception getting worse?
articles.summary: Operators are calling for urgent reform, as people across London struggle to make calls.
articles.body:
Mobile users across London say their mobile service is becoming increasingly unreliable, with reports of slow data speeds, failed connections and calls not getting through.

Mobile UK, the trade association representing the UK's major mobile networks, said London's mobile phone connectivity "continues to lag frustratingly behind other international hubs".

Data commissioned by the BBC England Data Unit found some of the worst areas were Liverpool Street and Covent Garden, where service proved to be extremely slow and unreliable during rush hour but worked normally during quieter periods.

So what impact does this lack of connectivity have on Londoners and their ability to earn a living, and what are the reasons behind it?

Virgin Media O2 recently called for urgent reform after being "forced" to switch off dozens of mobile sites across London because of new building developments.

Once a development receives planning consent, mobile operators are issued a notice-to-quit and must remove their antennas.

They are given an 18-month period to find a new site - although they say finding new antenna sites can take an average of two years. Temporary sites need to be found to maintain signal coverage.

Robert Joyce, director of mobile access engineering at Virgin Media O2, said: "If we can't find a replacement site before we remove that equipment then we can have a coverage hole in that location."

Operators say that thousands of people can be affected when a site is lost and cannot be replaced.

Mobile UK, which represents EE, O2, Three and Vodafone, said: "Delivering world-class coverage is an uphill battle in a high-density city where development constantly reshapes the skyline."

Network capacity is the total amount of data a network can handle at any given time.

Mobile users can have four or five signal bars but still experience slow uploads, undelivered messages and failed calls when a network is congested.

Philip Maguire, the founder and CEO of network measurement service Inakalum, said: "When the areas are busy, very often the networks don't have enough capacity to deal with all the data demands from users, and that's a capacity issue not a signal problem."

He added that most people would have "no chance" finding a reliable connection in the evening after leaving work despite the signal working in the early morning.

Philip surveyed three streets on behalf of the England Data Unit, all within a few minutes' walk of Covent Garden, on a weekday evening. He found that more than one in four data tests across EE, O2, Three and Vodafone failed outright.

Even when the networks worked, the data speed was found to be unreliable or slow - stuck under 15 Mbps (megabits per second). This meant that many people in the heart of the West End would struggle with basic tasks, such as loading maps or making video calls.

However, tests on the same streets at less busy times found that all four networks performed well, highlighting an issue of congestion rather than coverage.

Struggling for a signal in London Bridge

Adikalie Sumah, from Southwark, runs the shoe-cleaning business CureCleans and recently relocated to an office near London Bridge.

The move was designed to create easier access for customers and delivery drivers to drop off and collect their shoes, but he says the mobile signal is so bad he struggles to take calls in the office.

He uses EE, but the rest of the team use a range of network providers including O2 and Three.

Adikalie said: "When we're trying to contact customers to pick up and drop off their shoes, it's a bit of a struggle trying to get through to them."

They make and receive a lot of phone calls while taking orders and organising deliveries, and the poor service makes their work difficult.

At the moment, Adikalie manages this problem by taking phone calls outside the office and leaving all the doors and windows open to improve the signal, but says this means they sometimes get complaints from the neighbours.

He added that with winter approaching and because of the noise complaints, taking calls outside the office would no longer be an option. He said he had contacted his landlord about the issue but was told nothing could be done to improve it.

Adikalie mainly subcontracts to young people across Southwark, helping them to gain work experience, and while he hopes to keep offering these opportunities, he worries poor mobile service could hold the company back.

Joshua Folorunsho, 22, from Peckham, is a full-time content creator and an employee at CureCleans.

He is known as JTA across his social media platforms and creates content for the company.

"Obviously this is my livelihood so without it I'm not able to eat and put clothes on my back, so it's very important to me," he said.

Joshua, who has been using the services of Three since he was 15, said: "Sometimes when I call people it doesn't even ring, but I have service."

He said he struggled to find a reliable mobile signal when travelling across central London unless he's "lucky".

Joshua said he contacted a Three store in his local area but was told there was nothing they could do - and they said they also had poor mobile service.

Victoria Olaofe, 24, from Bermondsey, works as a sales representative near St Paul's, and she says that her poor mobile service means she misses out on pay.

"There have been occasions where my manager has tried to contact me, but I simply haven't received the calls or messages until much later. It's even affected things like clocking in on my phone."

Victoria gets paid by the hour and needs to clock into work using her phone, but her mobile data becomes unusable once she's in central London. This means she cannot clock in until hours later.

She said there did not seem to be any solution, so she just loses pay.

"I've also tried troubleshooting the issue. My mum even contacted Three after experiencing poor coverage in her area, and although my experience isn't identical to hers, it made me realise there may be a wider issue."

In response to a social media callout, Victoria said: "I realised I'm clearly not the only person experiencing this.

"It was reassuring to see that others are reporting similar issues, although it's concerning that so many people seem to be affected."

Experts say capacity shortfalls during busy times, housing developments and planning regulations are partly to blame, with rules varying across London's 33 councils - creating more challenges for network providers.

A spokesperson for London Councils, which represents all the local authorities in the capital, said: "The London Growth Plan and London Infrastructure Framework we developed jointly with the mayor highlight the importance of digital infrastructure and mobile connectivity.

"There is a range of factors behind the current connectivity problems, but boroughs take this issue seriously and are working with network providers and other partners to help resolve them."

Mobile UK said that mobile operators had invested "billions of pounds to upgrade their networks across London" and were committed to working with the government and local councils to improve mobile phone service.

The organisation also said it recognised that the Draft London Plan acknowledged the challenge housing developments posed to mobile operators in London, but it wants urgent policy reform on planning and a "unified framework that treats digital infrastructure as a priority".

A government spokesperson said: "Fast, reliable digital infrastructure is fundamental to a growing economy, keeping people connected wherever they live, work or commute. That's why we are working with industry to deliver our ambition for higher-quality standalone 5G coverage across all populated areas of the UK by 2030.

"We recognise that demand on mobile networks is growing, particularly in busy urban areas, and are reviewing planning rules and working through our Mobile Market Review to support investment, improve network performance and make it quicker and easier to build the infrastructure consumers and businesses need."

articles.title: A sealed early copy of Super Mario Bros. remained inside a Nintendo console bundle for decades; when discovered in 2026, it sold for $3 million
articles.summary: US News: A rare, sealed copy of Super Mario Bros. found in an unopened NES bundle sells for $3 million, setting a new auction record. Discover the unique features and its record-breaking sale.
articles.body: For nearly four decades, a copy of Super Mario Bros. was sealed inside an unopened Nintendo Entertainment System bundle. The copy was then discovered in 2026. The cartridge, preserved in its original packaging and accompanied by the Control Deck console with which it was originally bundled, eventually went to Heritage Auctions. It was sold for $3 million on 12 June 2026, setting a record for the highest price paid for a video game at a public auction.The cartridge received a PSA 9.6 A++ grade and was identified as a sealed example of Super Mario Bros.’ second production run. One of the things that made the find especially unusual was that it carried a short-lived gloss sticker seal associated with an early production variant. Meanwhile, the original console bundle itself had remained unopened. Contemporary reports suggest that only three sealed copies of this particular second-production variant were known, and the newly discovered one was considered the highest-graded of them.The cartridge belonged to an early production runThe NES and Super Mario Bros. dated to Nintendo’s early expansion of its home console business in the United States. It is, however, important to note that the console and cartridge should not be treated as though they came from the exact same production moment. Heritage Auctions’ description identifies the bundle as a 1985-styled USA Nintendo NES Control Deck release distributed in 1986. Meanwhile, the Super Mario Bros. cartridge itself is described as a second-production gloss-sticker example. Nintendo reportedly adopted the gloss sticker in early 1986, after the short-lived matte sticker used on launch copies from its October 1985 test market.The game itself is not a first-production copy. Instead, it is a second-production example which has been described as the earliest confirmed sealed copy because no sealed first-production example is currently known. Aside from the newly discovered one, the other two have received VGA 80 and Wata 9.4 A++ grades. The production history, therefore, provides an explanation for why a very common game could turn into an exceptionally rare collectable in one particular form.The game remained inside its original Nintendo bundleThe preservation of the cartridge was equally unconventional, as the original inner packaging remained intact. The console and its components had never even been removed from their plastic. The auction lot contained the Control Deck with which the Super Mario Bros. cartridge had originally been packaged. This indicates that the game had not been passed down between collectors; instead, it remained inside the original packaging, secured.Following its discovery two months prior to the sale, Heritage placed the cartridge and Control Deck together in its 12-13 June 2026 Video Games Signature Auction as Lot 28025. The auction house promoted the game as the earliest confirmed sealed edition of Super Mario Bros. and highlighted its condition alongside the circumstances of its discovery. The auction resulted in a $3 million sale. This had surpassed the previous $2 million record established by a private sale in 2021.The price of the copy is, therefore, tied to several aspects rather than just the age of the cartridge. Likely millions of people played the game, but this example belonged to a narrowly defined production variant, offering unparalleled historical provenance due to the un-boxing sequence. Additionally, its PSA 9.6 A++ grade further distinguished it from other surviving sealed copies of the same variant.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2024, a box of Alan Turing papers found gathering dust in a loft was nearly shredded during a house clearance; after being saved, it sold for £465,400 in 2025
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A collection of Alan Turing's papers, nearly shredded during a house clearance, was rescued and auctioned for a remarkable £465,400, revealing insights into the life of the legendary mathematician and computer science pioneer.
articles.body: A collection of papers written by the British mathematician Alan Turing was discovered in November 2024, buried among the personal effects of Norman Routledge, a Cambridge mathematician. According to Hansons Auctioneers, the family had been on the verge of shredding the papers before deciding to have them assessed. Seven months later, in June 2025, the lot sold for £465,400 at Hansons Rare Book Auctions in Staffordshire, more than triple the presale estimate.Norman Routledge received the papers as gifts from Turing's motherThis set of papers had belonged to Norman Routledge, who was a mathematician and longtime friend of Alan Turing from his days at King's College, Cambridge University. Turing, a brilliant mathematician who studied at King's and obtained his PhD in 1938, worked as a codebreaker at Bletchley Park during World War II and is known as a pioneer of computer science, according to Bletchley Park's official history of his life. After Turing died in 1954, his mother, Ethel Turing, passed a number of his academic offprints and personal papers on to Routledge, including a handwritten letter in which she apologized for being unable to send along Turing's paper on morphogenesis right away, a paper she evidently did send on later, since it later turned up in the same collection at auction.The papers sat untouched in a loft for yearsRoutledge passed away in 2013, leaving his sisters to deal with his possessions. Instead of throwing out the documents, one of his sisters decided to put the documents away in her loft, where they would go untouched for nearly ten years. She was later admitted to a care home, and when her daughters were sorting through her things, they came across the documents. According to Hansons Auctioneers, the daughters were seriously considering shredding the lot.A family reunion led to a valuation, November 2024It was only through the efforts of a cousin attending the family gathering in November 2024 that the documents were rescued; she recommended having the documents assessed before doing anything else. The family followed the recommendation by bringing the documents to a local valuation event in a carrier bag, and there the documents were evaluated by experts from the auction house Hansons, who referred the documents to their Rare Books Department in Lichfield, Staffordshire.The auction result far exceeded its estimate, June 2025The auction date was June 17, 2025, when bidding was done online, over the telephone, and face to face. Auctioneers had previously estimated that the most important pieces of the collection would go for £40,000 to £60,000 each, but the estimate was surpassed by the bidding very soon after its start. The original paper written by Turing in 1936 titled "On Computable Numbers, with an application to the Entscheidungsproblem," which was the paper that gave birth to the idea of the universal computer, was sold for £208,000.The original copy of Turing's Ph.D. thesis, titled 'Systems of Logic Based on Ordinals' and completed in 1938, went for £110,500. Together with other items from the collection, the sale totalled £465,400 including the buyer’s premium, which Hansons Auctioneers described as one of the strongest results for Turing material.The collection included Turing's only chemistry paperThe archive also included The Chemical Basis of Morphogenesis, Turing’s 1952 final paper and his only work in the field of chemistry. The auction house described the items as offprints, separate printings of scholarly papers produced in limited quantities for academic use. That scarcity helps explain why so few collections survive today.An archive preserved for future studyMuch of Turing's surviving written work, including drafts, letters, and lecture notes related to the papers sold in this collection, is preserved and catalogued at the Turing Digital Archive, managed by King’s College, Cambridge, which was not only the place where Turing studied but was also his fellowship. The collection is divided into eight groups covering his academic publications, wartime work on the Enigma machine, and personal correspondence, giving scholars a fuller view of his life than an auction listing can provide.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Gurgaon woman biker 'murder bid': Accused was returning from club, cousin instigated him to chase her
articles.summary: GURGAON: Kalyan Singh Bainsla, accused of chasing and ramming a woman biker in Gurgaon was allegedly returning from a club with his friends when the i.
articles.body: GURGAON: Kalyan Singh Bainsla, accused of chasing and ramming a woman biker in Gurgaon was allegedly returning from a club with his friends when the incident took place, sources told TOI.Bainsla was driving the white Maruti Ciaz when it allegedly knocked down Delhi-based biker Shivani Chauhan near the Sector 55-56 Rapid Metro station on Sunday.His cousin Lavnish, who was sitting in the passenger seat, was also arrested and sent to police custody.According to sources, Lavnish allegedly instigated Bainsla to chase Chauhan and also allegedly abused her during the incident.Police have described the incident as a "murder bid" and formed a five-member special investigation team (SIT) to investigate the case. The team is headed by the ACP (crime and women) and includes the SHO of Sector 56 police station, the Sohna crime branch in charge and two other police officers.Police to recreate the alleged chaseA local court on Wednesday sent Bainsla and Lavnish to police custody until Friday. Investigators said they would take the two accused to the spot during their custody to recreate the sequence of events.Police said they needed the custodial remand to prepare a crime script, establish the movements of the accused and determine the role of others who may have been involved.Chauhan told police that the driver of the white Ciaz, registration number HR-30-Y-4949, made indecent gestures at her before chasing her and deliberately ramming her motorcycle.Footage recorded by her motorcycle's camera shows the car repeatedly attempting to get alongside her Aprilia RS 457 before hitting it. The motorcycle then slid across the road as other vehicles continued to pass the scene.Case upgraded after biker's statementThe case was initially registered under sections 281 and 125 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against an unidentified driver.After Chauhan's statement and examination of the footage, police added sections 78, 79 and 109(1) of the BNS. The charges include an attempt-to-murder provision.Police took suo motu cognisance of the incident after a video posted by the Instagram account 'Rebelwheels_Sia' went viral on September 14. The video showed the white Ciaz and Chauhan's motorcycle.Chauhan later handed investigators a pen drive containing footage from her bike camera. Police also collected CCTV recordings from the GMDA and DLF covering Golf Course Road and the Metro station area between 6am and 8am on September 13.Investigators from the Sector 56 police station and Sohna crime branch searched for Bainsla at his Palwal residence and other locations before arresting him and Lavnish in Rajasthan on September 15. articles.title: ICE agent charged with assault, jailed in Minnesota
articles.summary: A federal immigration officer, Christian Castro, wanted on assault charges for shooting and ​wounding a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis was arrested there on Wednesday.
articles.body: A federal immigration officer wanted on assault charges for shooting and ​wounding a Venezuelan man in Minneapolis was arrested there on Wednesday, eight months after a confrontation that became a flashpoint over ‌US President Donald Trump’s deportation sweeps. Immigration and Customs Enforcement agent Christian Castro was taken into custody by agents of the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension in downtown Minneapolis and was booked into the Hennepin County jail on his outstanding arrest warrant, the agency said. Castro had been released on bond from federal custody earlier this month, after an initial appearance in a District Court ​in McAllen, Texas, on charges of lying to investigators about the circumstances of the January 14 shooting. Under an agreement with Minnesota law enforcement, ​Castro voluntarily drove to Minneapolis from Texas to turn himself in to state authorities at his attorney’s office but ended ⁠up being arrested minutes before he was due to arrive, the lawyer, Daniel Gerdts told Reuters. Another lawyer representing the ICE agent, Rolando Cantu, said his ​client always had intended to answer to the charges in Minneapolis. He disputed Hennepin County prosecutors’ assertions that Castro might flee to Mexico, saying, “He wants his ​day in court.” Case stems from Operation Metro surge The federal indictment charging Castro with making false statements marked the first Justice Department prosecution of a federal law enforcement officer accused of wrongdoing arising from the massive Minneapolis ICE deployment dubbed Operation Metro Surge. That operation, part of Trump’s wider immigration crackdown, drew weeks of protests and clashes between ICE and demonstrators, leading to ​the fatal shootings of two U.S. citizens by federal agents. Castro already faced state assault charges in Minnesota stemming from the confrontation in which he shot Julio ​Cesar Sosa-Celis, a Venezuelan national, in the leg through the door of the man’s apartment while children were present inside the home. The state charges also include false reporting of ‌a crime ⁠after Castro allegedly told superiors at the Department of Homeland Security that Sosa-Celis and others attacked him with a snow shovel and broom, which was disproved by video evidence. Initial efforts to arrest Castro were thwarted when the ICE agent returned to his home state of Texas, leading Minnesota officials to issue a warrant for his arrest. Castro was apprehended by Texas Rangers, but Texas Governor Greg Abbott, a Republican and supporter of Trump’s mass deportation sweeps, refused to sign ​extradition papers sent by Minnesota Governor Tim ​Walz, a Democrat. Abbott questioned whether ⁠Castro could be considered a fugitive from justice, and thus subject to extradition, because DHS had reassigned him to his home state of Texas after the Minneapolis shooting. The ICE agent ultimately spent 90 days in a Texas county jail and ​was released on August 27 after a federal judge in Texas denied a request from Minnesota to immediately ​order his extradition. Castro ⁠was re-arrested in Texas following his federal grand jury indictment in early September. DHS has suspended Castro from ICE, and a person familiar with the case has said a civil rights investigation into the Sosa-Celis shooting had been opened. Castro was expected to make his first state court appearance in Minneapolis on Thursday. He will then make ⁠an initial appearance ​in a District Court in neighboring St. Paul, the state capital, on Friday morning to ​face charges in the federal indictment. “Governor Abbott’s attempt to shield Mr. Castro from accountability has failed. We look forward to commencing our prosecution,” Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty, who brought the state ​case, said in a statement.

articles.title: EU announces plan to restrict social media access for children
articles.summary: Under the plans, only children over 15 would be able to set up their own social media accounts.
articles.body:
The EU has announced plans to restrict social media access for under-15s across its member states, in a bid to increase wellbeing and tackle online safety.

Under the plans, there would be a gradual approach to children using social media which would include banning under 13s from accessing platforms.

Those aged 13 to 15 would only be able to access platforms for an hour per day via "mini accounts" set up through their parent or guardian's social media account.

The European Commission said social media companies would need to prove platforms were safe by design or face fines of up to 6% of their global sales. EU chief Ursula von der Leyen said the move would "put parents back in the driving seat".

She added the legislation - called the EU Kids Act - would give parents "the tools to help their children navigate a safer world".

The restrictions would not just affect well-known apps such as TikTok, Instagram, and Snapchat but also YouTube and other video sharing platforms as well as AI chatbots and online games.

"Too many children are being exposed too early to an online world they are not ready to navigate - an environment where bullying can follow you home, where every mistake can be recorded forever," von der Leyen said.

Under the act, only children aged 15 and over would be able to set up their own social media accounts.

But von der Leyen told the EU Parliament on Thursday that "an age limit does not mean letting tech companies off the hook for the content on the platform".

She added that under the legislation - if it is approved - companies would be required to submit detailed child safety plans.

"For every person under 18, the platforms must follow the principle of safety by design, no toxic or addictive features, no traps, etc," she said.

Some individual EU countries have already announced their own plans to restrict social media for children, including France and Spain.

The proposed EU-wide legislation would supersede those, and member states will not be able to opt out from what would be a legally binding regulation.

It is understood the Commission has warned some member states they would need to repeal any national laws passed before the EU Kids Act comes into effect.

The new plans need to be agreed by EU member states and approved by the European Parliament.

Already there are questions about how this EU-wide legislation would be enforced and the plans are likely to face opposition in the months to come.

France provides an indication of how the path ahead could be bumpy as individual member states may try to strengthen or weaken the proposals.

The Macron government drew up legislation for a ban on social media for under-15s but last month the country's top court blocked it, ruling that it infringed upon freedom of expression.

French ministers have now amended their original plans.

Some critics of social media bans for children cite privacy concerns.

They worry about teenagers being forced to submit personal information as they go through an age verification process to prove they are old enough to access platforms.

The Commission has said age would be verified using the EU's preexisting age verification app, and no personal data would be collected or shared.

Social media companies will also make their position on the restrictions clear as the act is debated in the months to come.

Von der Leyen had previously proposed a social media "delay" for children in Europe, saying in May that "the discussion about a minimum age for social media can no longer be ignored".

The policy, formally outlined on Thursday, was also trailed in the EU chief's annual address on Wednesday.

In July, the EU said Meta must change the "addictive" design of Facebook and Instagram or face a heavy fine.

In preliminary findings, the European Commission said features such as infinite scroll, autoplaying videos and personalised recommendations could encourage "compulsive use", particularly among children and teens.

A spokesperson for the tech giant told the BBC it disagreed with the findings "which don't accurately take into account the significant steps we've taken to protect teens".

In a separate case, Meta agreed in August to a $18bn (£13.3bn) settlement with US states and territories to resolve claims that Facebook and Instagram harmed children. It denied any wrongdoing as part of the settlement.

The European Commission said its proposed legislation built on findings from its special panel on child safety online, which recommended age-appropriate regulation for children, with different guidance for each age group.

It also cited recent EU survey data , which found 92% of respondents considered the need to strengthen children's protection online as a top policy priority.

Von der Leyen said the Commission had "looked at Australia" - which banned social media platforms for under-16s last year - when putting together the proposal.

The ban has been difficult for the country to enforce, with its Communications Minister Anika Wells admitting earlier this month that so far no tech firm had been fined despite research showing many under-16s were still on platforms.

A similar ban for under-16s is set to come into force in the UK in spring next year.

articles.title: ‘Poor bear the impact’: Sugar prices soar in India, souring festive season
articles.summary: India is one of the world’s largest sugar consumers, but usually produces much more.
articles.body:
Jai Krishan, a 43-year-old labourer from Bihar in northern India, has saved 15,000 rupees ($160) to travel home from Indian-administered Kashmir, where he works, to celebrate Diwali with his family in November.

Each year, he buys boxes of sweets — laddu, barfi and kaju katli — to take home as gifts for his family and friends. He spends about $35 just on sweets for Diwali, he says, as he prepares afternoon tea for himself and his roommates in their rented accommodation in the Hawal area of Srinagar, Indian-administered Kashmir’s largest city.

“For someone from a lower-middle-class family, this is a lot of money. But Diwali is one of the most important festivals for Hindus and you cannot skip celebrating it,” he says.

This year, though, Krishan fears he may have to cut back on other purchases — such as toys and clothes — to keep his limited budget under control. The price of sugar has risen sharply in recent months, with retail prices reaching as high as 75 rupees ($0.79) per kilogramme (2.2 pounds) — up from 40 rupees in September 2025 — in some markets, raising concerns that the cost of sweets could also increase.

“I can reduce my spending on clothes or other things, but I cannot return home without bringing sweets for my family,” Krishan said.

The price rise comes as India enters its festival season. Celebrations begin in late August with festivals such as Ganesh Chaturthi and Onam, before gathering pace in October and November with Navratri, Durga Puja, Dussehra and Diwali, popularly known as the festival of lights.

India’s sweets sector is worth more than $1.1bn, with peak festive sales accounting for more than 40 percent of annual revenue. Traditional sweets can contain 30 to 60 percent sugar by weight, making sugar a major ingredient. India is the world’s largest consumer and second-largest producer of sugar.

The country consumes between 29 million and 32 million metric tonnes of sugar each year, roughly 15 percent of global consumption. But it produces about 20 percent of the world’s sugar, second only to Brazil — an amount that means that the country usually has enough supplies of sugar for its needs, with some to spare for exports.

Sugar production, according to government data, is expected to be about 30.6 million tonnes in the current season, which runs from October 2025 to September 2026. This is 11 percent lower than the government’s earlier estimate of 34.3 million tonnes.

The government attributes the lower production mainly to a decline in sugarcane cultivation and lower rainfall during the El Nino weather pattern. It has also accused hoarders of storing extra sugar once the effects of El Nino became clear, to further tighten supplies in a bid to earn extra profits.

But Mukesh Chandra, a sugarcane farmer from Punjab, says several other factors have contributed to the fall in production and the rise in sugar prices.

He points to a shift by some farmers from sugarcane to other crops, high labour costs coupled with low returns from sugarcane farming, and the diversion of sugarcane to ethanol production as among those reasons.

“These factors have led to a decline in the amount of sugarcane available for processing, putting pressure on sugar supplies and pushing up prices,” Chandra told Al Jazeera. “Why would a farmer cultivate a product that is going to give him less returns?”

The Indian government, however, has rejected the claim that diverting sugarcane to ethanol production under its ethanol blending programme has contributed to the surge in sugar prices. It pointed to figures showing that the share of sugar diverted to ethanol has fallen from about 12 percent in 2022-23 to about 9 percent in 2025-26, with nearly three-quarters of India’s ethanol now made from grains such as maize.

India introduced ethanol blending to reduce its dependence on expensive crude oil imports, strengthen energy security and increase farmers’ incomes by creating a market for surplus crops. The initiative is also intended to reduce vehicle emissions and support the country’s broader decarbonisation goals.

Regardless of the Indian government’s assertions, Chandra argues that the economic logic of sugarcane farming works against cultivators.

He estimates that producing 100kg of sugar costs about 470 rupees ($4.90), including expenses for labour, irrigation, cultivation and transportation, as well as the extraction of sugarcane juice and its processing into sugar. But the return is only about 416 rupees, leaving farmers with a loss of approximately 54 rupees per 100kg. He said sugarcane farmers also do not receive the same level of support available to farmers growing crops such as paddy — particularly with fertilisers, diesel and electricity.

The United States-Israeli war on Iran has also complicated economic equations for farmers, with fuel prices — and so, electricity costs — rising. The inflation due to the war “has added a further burden on our shoulders,” Chandra said. “The rise in fuel prices has increased the cost of running water pumps used to irrigate sugarcane fields, adding to farmers’ expenses at a time when their margins are already low.”

Suresh Pal, another sugarcane farmer from the state of Uttar Pradesh, agrees that sugarcane production is declining. He attributes the current shortage and price rise to a combination of agricultural and climate-related challenges faced by farmers in the state.

Farmers in Uttar Pradesh remain heavily dependent on the Co-0238 variety of sugarcane, which, Pal said, has become increasingly vulnerable to diseases such as red rot fungus and pest attacks. He added that continuous cultivation and the heavy use of chemicals have also contributed to soil degradation, while the crop’s high water requirements have put further pressure on the state’s groundwater resources.

“We are facing problems from many sides. The varieties we depend on are becoming vulnerable to diseases, the soil is losing its strength and water is becoming harder to manage,” Pal told Al Jazeera. “And at the same time, the cost of farming is increasing. Fertiliser, pesticides, labour and irrigation are all becoming expensive,” he added.

For small farmers, Pal believes, the financial strain is made worse by delayed payments from sugar mills, leaving them with little money to invest in better seeds, modern farming methods and new technologies. “When the mills delay our payments, how can a small farmer invest more in his fields?” Pal said. “Our costs keep rising, but the money we earn from farming is not increasing at the same pace. This is making it difficult for people like me to continue cultivating sugarcane.”

To manage domestic supply, the government has authorised the duty-free import of one million tonnes of raw sugar, with a cap on rates, until October 31, 2026. The move is aimed at easing supply pressures ahead of the festival season.

“The measure is best understood as a price ceiling rather than a price cut,” said Sanjay Kumar, professor of economics at Delhi University. The government waived heavy import duties to allow the import of sugar at about $0.55 per kg. “That price now limits how high domestic sugar can go, because once imported sugar is cheaper, no mill can hold its own price above the landed cost for long,” Kumar added.

But so far, that strategy doesn’t seem to be working.

That, Kumar said, is because the imports are of raw sugar; the domestic Indian market demand is primarily for refined sugar.

Aman Jaswal, a resident of Patna in Bihar, said sweets were costing 15 to 20 percent more this year. “Sweets are closely tied to happiness in Indian culture. Whether it is Diwali, a wedding or a religious occasion, we rarely celebrate without them,” Jaswal said. “Even prasad [the sweets offered during religious rituals] is shared among people. Gifting sweets is a way of sharing happiness and it has become part of our celebrations and relationships.”

Back in Srinagar, Krishan, the labourer, has already started thinking about what he can sacrifice this year to be able to afford sweets for his family back home.

He has taken to walking to work, instead of taking public transport.

“My workplace is about eight kilometres from my room but I walk to save 50 rupees ($0.52) a day for the happiness of my family,” he said. “What difference does it make to the rich? They will celebrate the festival with great pomp and show anyway. It is poor people like me who will bear the impact.”

articles.title: Helen Jenner likely to take over as Reform Wales leader, sources tell BBC
articles.summary: Reform's Welsh deputy leader is the favourite to take over from Dan Thomas, who was arrested on Sunday.
articles.body:
Reform is likely to appoint Helen Jenner to take over from Dan Thomas as the party's Welsh leader, sources have told BBC Wales.

It is understood she is the favourite to replace Thomas, who quit following an arrest on suspicion of assault, and that "very senior" Reform figures had backed her.

Jenner, an MS for Bangor Conwy Môn, is the party's interim Welsh leader and was Thomas' deputy.

Thomas stood down after he was arrested and bailed by police at the weekend on suspicion of assault and controlling coercive behaviour.

Meanwhile, chief whip Llŷr Powell told BBC Wales that he has ruled himself out of standing for the leadership.

Thomas has not been suspended and continues to represent Reform in the Senedd as MS for Casnewydd Islwyn.

Jenner is yet to speak publicly about her intentions.

The party's health spokesperson James Evans claimed on Wednesday he had majority support in the group but decided not to stand after speaking to his family.

If there is more than one candidate it is expected there will be a secret ballot of Reform MSs - but no vote of the membership.

Thomas was appointed by Nigel Farage in February.

Helen Jenner is a former English teacher who was born in the south Wales town of Neath and grew up on Anglesey.

In a BBC Walescast podcast episode during the summer Jenner, a Welsh speaker, said that people online had told her she had "no right" to attend the National Eisteddfod , because of her membership of Reform.

Jenner stood for the Brexit Party at the 2019 UK general election, and was previously a member of UKIP, when it was led by current Reform UK leader Nigel Farage.

On Walescast she said Farage had helped her become engaged in politics.

"It was seeing him, and then watching his YouTube clips in the European Parliament and everything: I've never seen anybody so animated

"I felt he was really principled and I suddenly thought 'oh, I actually care about politics now'."
